advances: The proposed leading selection cost \(\kappa\sqrt{nk}\) is necessary, including for strictly positive rational rows. Disjoint blocks have an exact minimum; a positive rational perturbation preserves the asymptotic lower bound with leading constant one whenever the block size is large compared with \(\kappa^2\). The perturbed rows also arise at the unique equal-rate dual minimizer of the accepted positive-resource construction. Consequently its elementary inflation choice \(\kappa_k=4096\lceil2\sqrt{k}\rceil\) necessarily pays selected-coordinate loss of order \(k\sqrt n\log k\) on an explicit family. This calibrates the resource implication of simultaneous selection without duplicating an upper-bound theorem or claiming a counterexample to the locked problem.

proof:
Write \(q_r=|I\cap B_r|\). For the disjoint rows, (1) is exactly \(\kappa^2(m-q_r)\le q_r^2\). The polynomial \(q^2+\kappa^2q-\kappa^2m\) is strictly increasing for \(q\ge0\); its positive root is \((\sqrt{\kappa^4+4\kappa^2m}-\kappa^2)/2\). It lies strictly between zero and \(m\). Thus each block requires the ceiling in (2), and choosing exactly that many coordinates from each block attains (2).

Dividing the positive root by \(\kappa\sqrt m\) gives \(\sqrt{1+\kappa^2/(4m)}-\kappa/(2\sqrt m)\), which tends to one when \(m/\kappa^2\to\infty\). The ceiling contributes at most \(1/(\kappa\sqrt m)\) to this ratio, which tends to zero because \(\kappa\ge1\) and \(m/\kappa^2\to\infty\). Since \(\kappa\sqrt{nk}=k\kappa\sqrt m\), the claimed exact asymptotic follows.

For the positive rational perturbation, the unselected coordinates inside \(B_r\) contribute \(m-q_r\) to the left side of (1), while the selected row sum is \(q_r+\varepsilon(|I|-q_r)\le q_r+\varepsilon n\). Feasibility therefore implies \(q_r+\varepsilon n\ge\kappa\sqrt{m-q_r}\). Let \(\rho=(\sqrt{\kappa^4+4\kappa^2m}-\kappa^2)/2\), so \(\rho=\kappa\sqrt{m-\rho}\). If \(q_r<\rho-\varepsilon n\), then \(q_r+\varepsilon n<\rho\) but \(\kappa\sqrt{m-q_r}>\kappa\sqrt{m-\rho}=\rho\), a contradiction. Thus \(q_r\ge\rho-\varepsilon n\). Summing over the blocks gives \(|I|\ge k\rho-k\varepsilon n=k\rho-k/n\). Also \(\sqrt{\kappa^4+4\kappa^2m}\ge2\kappa\sqrt m\), so \(\rho\ge\kappa\sqrt m-\kappa^2/2\), proving (3). The relative correction in (3) tends to zero when \(m/\kappa^2\to\infty\), independently of \(k\).

We next verify the resource realization using only the objects and dual construction of accepted fact `41d185e7405de421`, with the exact normalization (4). Every column of \(A\) has sum \(1+(k-1)\varepsilon\), and every row has sum \(m[1+(k-1)\varepsilon]\). Set \(\lambda_r=s/[1+(k-1)\varepsilon]\) for every row. Then \(\sum_r\lambda_ra_{ri}=s\) for every coordinate.

The predecessor's convex objective is \(\mathcal F(\lambda)=\lambda\cdot R+\sum_i\phi(\sum_r\lambda_ra_{ri})\), with \(\phi(t)=\max\{0,\psi(t)-\psi(h)\}\) and \(\psi(t)=\tfrac13\log F(e^{-3t})\). On \(0<t<h\), it has \(\phi'(t)=-\mu(t)\) and \(\phi''(t)=3\operatorname{Var}_{Q_{e^{-t}}}(u)>0\). Positivity of this variance follows directly from (4), since both \(u=0\) and \(u=1\) have positive probability. At the stated multipliers,
\[
\frac{\partial\mathcal F}{\partial\lambda_r}
=R_r-\mu(s)\sum_i a_{ri}=0
\qquad(1\le r\le k).
\tag{6}
\]
The positive multiplier vector is therefore a global minimizer of the convex objective on the nonnegative orthant.

It is unique. For \(n>1\) we have \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and if a vector \(v\in\mathbb R^k\) annihilates all columns, then for every block label \(r\), \((1-\varepsilon)v_r+\varepsilon\sum_a v_a=0\). Subtracting any two equations makes all \(v_r\) equal; substituting back gives \([1+(k-1)\varepsilon]v_r=0\), hence \(v=0\). For \(n=1\), necessarily \(k=m=1\), and \(A=(1)\) also has full row rank. Thus the Hessian at the proposed minimizer is \(3\operatorname{Var}_{Q_{e^{-s}}}(u)AA^{\mathsf T}\), which is positive definite. It remains positive definite in a neighborhood where all rates lie in \((0,h)\). Were there a second global minimizer, convexity would force \(\mathcal F\) to be constant on the connecting segment, contradicting this strict curvature near the first minimizer. Since the rates are strictly below \(h\), the predecessor's primal coordinates all equal \(\mu(s)\), with no tied or fractional coordinates, proving \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The normalized row weights are \(a_{ri}\mu_i=\mu(s)w_{ri}\). The common positive scalar cancels from (1), so (3) applies to these very row weights.

Finally substitute \(\kappa=\kappa_k\) in (3) and multiply by the positive \(b_k\), proving (5). As \(k\to\infty\), \(\kappa_k/\sqrt k\to8192\) and \(b_k/\log k\to3/2\). If also \(m/k\to\infty\), then \(m/\kappa_k^2\to\infty\), so the right side of (5) is \((1-o(1))b_k\kappa_k\sqrt{nk}=(1-o(1))12288\,k\sqrt n\log k\). Division by \(n\) gives the necessary condition stated after (5) for bounding this selected-coordinate price by \(O(n)\).

For an entirely explicit family where this estimate's loss exceeds every fixed multiple of \(n\), take integers \(t\ge1\), set \(k=4^t\), \(m=kt\), and \(n=k^2t\), and use the strictly positive rational rows above. Then \(\kappa_k=8192\sqrt k\), \(m/k=t\to\infty\), and \(k\log k/\sqrt n=(\log4)\sqrt t\to\infty\). Hence (5) implies \(b_k|I|/n\to\infty\). In equation (17) of accepted fact `41d185e7405de421`, the coordinate baseline is \((8/27)^n=4^{-n}\exp[n\log(32/27)]\); on this family the necessary selected-coordinate penalty alone eventually exceeds that linear baseline gain. Thus that lower-bound estimate, with this elementary inflation rule, cannot certify a fixed exponential improvement over \(4^{-n}\) on the explicit family merely by improving the subset search. It does not assert that the actual moment is small.
statement:
Let \(k,m\ge1\) be integers, put \(n=km\), and partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into \(k\) blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), each of size \(m\). Let \(\kappa\ge1\) be real. A subset \(I\) is called feasible for rows \(w_1,\ldots,w_k\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n\) when
\[
\sum_{i\notin I}w_{ri}^2\le\frac1{\kappa^2}\left(\sum_{i\in I}w_{ri}\right)^2
\qquad(1\le r\le k).
\tag{1}
\]
The following three assertions hold.

For the disjoint rows \(w_{ri}=1\) on \(B_r\) and \(w_{ri}=0\) elsewhere, the exact minimum feasible cardinality is
\[
k\left\lceil\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^4+4\kappa^2m}-\kappa^2}{2}\right\rceil.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, along any sequence with \(m/\kappa^2\longrightarrow\infty\), this minimum divided by \(\kappa\sqrt{nk}\) tends to one.

For strictly positive rational rows, put \(\varepsilon=1/n^2\), let \(w_{ri}=1\) on \(B_r\), and let \(w_{ri}=\varepsilon\) elsewhere. Every feasible \(I\) satisfies
\[
|I|\ge k\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^4+4\kappa^2m}-\kappa^2}{2}-\frac{k}{n}
\ge\kappa\sqrt{nk}-\frac{\kappa^2k}{2}-\frac{k}{n}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus no uniform bound can replace the proposed leading \(\kappa\sqrt{nk}\) term by a quantity of smaller order in the regime \(m/\kappa^2\to\infty\). This is a lower-bound calibration, not a family refuting every constant in the proposed upper bound.

The positive rows in (3) can be realized, up to a common positive scalar, as the row weights \(a_{ri}\mu_i\) on \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) in accepted fact `41d185e7405de421`. More precisely, take its resource matrix \(A=(w_{ri})\), choose any \(s\in(0,h)\), where \(h=\log3\), and take all capacities equal to \(m[1+(k-1)\varepsilon]\mu(s)\). Here \(\mu(s)\) is exactly the mean of the predecessor's coordinate law
\[
Q_{e^{-s}}(u)=\frac{(2u+1)^2e^{-3su}}{F(e^{-3s})},\qquad
F(z)=\frac{1+6z+z^2}{(1-z)^3},\qquad u\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
\tag{4}
\]
The predecessor's dual objective has the unique minimizer with every multiplier equal to \(s/[1+(k-1)\varepsilon]\); every coordinate rate is \(s\), so \(\mu_i=\mu(s)>0\) and every coordinate belongs to \(I_0\).

For these resources, consider the same elementary inflation rule \(\kappa_k=4096\lceil2\sqrt k\rceil\) and the same selected-coordinate penalty \(b_k|I|\) in equation (17) of accepted fact `41d185e7405de421`, where \(b_k=6+\log(8\kappa_k^3)\). Every subset satisfying (1) with \(\kappa=\kappa_k\) has
\[
b_k|I|\ge b_k\left(\kappa_k\sqrt{nk}-\frac{\kappa_k^2k}{2}-\frac{k}{n}\right).
\tag{5}
\]
Along \(k\to\infty\) and \(m/k\to\infty\), the right side is \((1-o(1))12288\,k\sqrt n\log k\). Hence the selected-coordinate penalty in this particular estimate cannot be bounded uniformly by a fixed multiple of \(n\) unless \(k\log k=O(\sqrt n)\) in that regime. This is a limitation of the displayed inflation-and-normalization estimate, not a necessary condition for the actual reflection moment or for weak Oertel.
